drhp.business: The Company's core business is the manufacture of woven and knitted elastic tapes; its stated vision is to become a leading manufacturer of woven and knitted elastic tapes. It operates in India and, through its wholly owned subsidiary Premco Global Vietnam Company Limited, in Vietnam. The annual report under review is the Company's 42nd, for the financial year ended 31st March 2026.
drhp.end_markets: Export markets — the Company incurs export-related expenses and its consolidated performance was stated to be affected by tariff measures imposed by the United States of America|Vietnam — operations conducted through the wholly owned subsidiary Premco Global Vietnam Co. Ltd.
drhp.expansion: The routed sections disclose no named capex or expansion project, no commissioning or ramp-up timeline, and no plant/capacity addition. The only forward capital-deployment statement is a reinvestment intent: the Board proposed no transfer to the General Reserve and the entire earnings for FY 2025-26, after payment of dividend, are to be retained in the Profit & Loss Account 'to support future business expansion, technological upgradation, and strategic initiatives'. There was no change in the nature of business during the year and no company became or ceased to be a subsidiary, joint venture …

litigation.note: The Directors state that during FY 2025-26 no significant or material order was passed by any regulator, court or tribunal that impacts the going-concern status of the Company or will have a bearing on its future operations. No application was made and no proceeding was pending under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016. No cases were filed or pending during the year under the PoSH Act, 2013. No one-time settlement was done during the year.

drhp.one_liner: Premco Global Limited is a Mumbai-headquartered manufacturer of woven and knitted elastic tapes, incorporated in 1986 as a family-led enterprise and now a professionally managed listed company with a wholly owned manufacturing subsidiary in Vietnam.

risks.note: The Directors' Report attributes the decline in consolidated profitability primarily to the impact of tariff measures imposed by the United States of America. This is the only cause management names for the consolidated shortfall, making trade-policy action on the group's export markets a structural, recurring exposure rather than a one-off.
risks.risk: US tariff exposure on the export/overseas business

risks.note: Management explicitly cites 'prevailing geopolitical uncertainties, including war-like situations in various regions, which adversely affected global trade and business conditions' as a driver of the consolidated profit decline — an exogenous demand and logistics risk it cannot mitigate internally.
risks.risk: Geopolitical uncertainty and war-like situations disrupting global trade

risks.note: The Directors' Report states that standalone revenue from operations decreased while other income rose substantially, and that the group-level result diverged sharply from the standalone result. Earnings quality therefore rests partly on non-operating income. (No figures reproduced here — the underlying table is a primary financial statement.)
risks.risk: Dependence of standalone profitability on other income rather than operations

risks.note: The consolidated result is materially different from the standalone result, indicating the overseas subsidiary carries a significant share of group activity; a shock to that single geography flows straight through to consolidated earnings.
risks.risk: Concentration of the group's operations in a single overseas subsidiary

risks.note: Because the Company was not among the top 1,000 listed entities by market capitalisation as on 31st March 2026, constituting a Risk Management Committee under Regulation 21 of SEBI LODR was not mandatory and none was constituted. Risk oversight rests on the full Board's periodic review rather than a dedicated committee.
The Company states it did not obtain any credit rating during FY 2025-26, so there is no third-party assessment of its credit quality for lenders or investors to reference.

The AR describes an 'adequate and effective Risk Management Framework' in generic terms — identification, evaluation, mitigation and monitoring reviewed periodically by the Board — but the routed text contains no MD&A 'Risks and Concerns' section enumerating the specific risks or their mitigations, so the framework cannot be assessed against named exposures.
risks.risk: Reliance on a Board-level risk framework with no disclosed risk register
